result.result:
The Master's ETA of 2025-01-31T11:00:00Z for Sept-Iles is consistent — check_eta computes 2025-01-31T12:18:00Z from the 1,503.8 nm distance to go at 12.5 kn, within the 2-hour tolerance (difference 1.3 h). No ETA notice is due now: the last notice was sent 5 days before arrival (2025-01-25, ETA 2025-01-31T06:00:00Z), and at 4.96 days to arrival the next notice (3 days, to the agent) has not fallen due.

The remarks explain the stop, so no query to the Master is needed. check_stoppage confirms the stop agrees with the report: main engine stopped 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z to 2025-01-26T11:40:00Z (5.5 h), VLSFO 1.1 t used, with the reported speed over the remaining 18.5 steaming hours matching the 231.3 nm distance run.

The simulated hire statement (figures made up for this simulation; a real voyage management system would give its own) shows hire deducted of US$2,177.08 for 5.5 h at US$9,500/day, plus 1.1 t VLSFO at US$660 charged to the owners' account — total US$2,837.08 for the owner.

Judgement on the CP off-hire clause: loss of time from breakdown of machinery or equipment preventing full working of the vessel is off hire. The choked fuel oil filters stopping the main engine fit this, so the stop is off hire. However, since the sludge may lie in the fuel the charterer supplied, the owner may argue the point — that claim is the operator's to make, and this should not come as a surprise.

The operator should decide whether to put MV TORMAR SPRING off hire for 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z–2025-01-26T11:40:00Z and notify the owner, Tormar Bulk Carriers. On a yes: (a) a voyage management system entry for the off-hire period would be proposed via propose_entry (kind off_hire, reason stating the main engine stop, about off_hire), and (b) an e-mail to the owner's vessel technical management giving the period and reason and asking for the engine log extract for the stop.

draft.body:
Dear Sirs,

We wish to place MV TORMAR SPRING off hire for the main-engine stop from 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z to 2025-01-26T11:40:00Z (5.5 h), caused by fuel oil filters choked with sludge stirred up in heavy weather. The filters were cleaned and the engine was restarted.

Hire deducted: US$2,177.08 for 5.5 h at US$9,500/day.  
Additional charge: 1.1 t VLSFO at US$660, charged to the owners' account.  
Total for the owner: US$2,837.08.

Please provide the engine log extract for the stop.

Best regards,
Operations
